findings.title: GraphQL resolver uses inline object mapping instead of dedicated mapper/DTO
findings.description: The EconomicDataResolver manually maps database entities to GraphQL models inline within resolver methods (lines 28-41, 48-63, 79-94). NestJS best practices recommend using dedicated mapper classes or AutoMapper to separate transformation logic from resolver logic, improving testability and maintainability.
findings.suggested_issue: Extract inline object mappings to a dedicated EconomicDataMapper class with methods like toDataPointModel() and toFetchConfigModel() to improve separation of concerns and testability.

findings.title: Repeated mapping logic duplicated across multiple resolver methods
findings.description: The item mapping logic (slug, displayName, groupLabel, defaultUnit, metadata) is duplicated in getEconomicData (lines 34-40), economicDataFetchConfigs (lines 56-62), and updateEconomicDataFetchConfig (lines 87-93). This violates DRY principle and increases maintenance burden.
findings.snippet:
item: {
  slug: point.item.slug,
  displayName: point.item.displayName,
  groupLabel: point.item.groupLabel ?? undefined,
  defaultUnit: point.item.defaultUnit ?? null,
  metadata: (point.item.metadata as Record<string, unknown> | null) ?? null
}
findings.suggested_issue: Create a shared mapEconomicDataItem() helper function or use a mapper class to eliminate the duplicated item mapping logic across resolver methods.

findings.title: Type assertion used for metadata without runtime validation
findings.description: The resolver casts metadata using 'as Record<string, unknown>' without runtime type validation (lines 39, 61, 92). This bypasses TypeScript's type safety and could lead to runtime errors if the database contains unexpected metadata shapes.
findings.snippet: metadata: (point.item.metadata as Record<string, unknown> | null) ?? null
findings.suggested_issue: Use a runtime validation library (zod, class-validator) or create a type guard function to validate metadata shape before casting, ensuring type safety at runtime.

findings.title: React hook uses Map data structure causing potential re-render issues
findings.description: useEconomicData hook returns EconomicSeriesMap (Map<string, EconomicSeriesGroup>) which uses nested Map structures (lines 43-88). React's shallow comparison cannot detect changes inside Map objects, potentially causing missed re-renders or unnecessary re-renders when the Map reference changes but content is identical.
findings.suggested_issue: Consider using plain objects or arrays instead of Map for React state to ensure proper shallow comparison. Alternatively, use a stable serialization approach or implement custom comparison logic.

findings.title: Tooltip formatter uses 'any' type annotation
findings.description: The ECharts tooltip formatter callback uses 'any' type (line 212) which bypasses TypeScript's type checking. This is an anti-pattern that reduces type safety and IDE support.
findings.suggested_issue: Import and use ECharts' CallbackDataParams type or define a proper interface for the tooltip formatter parameters to maintain type safety.

findings.title: Hardcoded fallback string bypasses i18n system
findings.description: The economic-chart-card component has a hardcoded English fallback string (lines 89-91) that bypasses the i18n translation system when translation keys are missing. This creates inconsistent user experience for non-English users.
findings.suggested_issue: Remove the hardcoded fallback and ensure all translation keys exist in the i18n resource files. Use the t() function's defaultValue option consistently instead of post-hoc string checking.

findings.title: Inline style objects in JSX cause unnecessary re-renders
findings.description: The economic-chart-card component creates new style objects inline within JSX (lines 151-157, 124-125). These objects are recreated on every render, potentially causing unnecessary child component re-renders.
findings.suggested_issue: Extract inline style objects to useMemo hooks or CSS-in-JS styled components to prevent unnecessary object recreation on each render.

findings.title: Service method has excessive cyclomatic complexity
findings.description: The ensureCatalog() method in AkshareService (lines 169-315) has high cyclomatic complexity with deeply nested conditionals and multiple database operations. This makes the code difficult to test, understand, and maintain.
findings.suggested_issue: Refactor ensureCatalog() into smaller, focused methods: ensureCategories(), ensureDataItems(), ensureFetchConfigs(). Each method should handle a single responsibility.

findings.title: Magic strings used for parser type discrimination
findings.description: The parsePayload() method uses string literals ('latest', 'timeseries', 'macro', etc.) for parser type discrimination (lines 731-754). These magic strings are error-prone and lack IDE autocomplete support.
findings.suggested_issue: Define a const enum or string literal union type for parser types (e.g., PARSER_TYPES.LATEST) and use it consistently across definitions and service code.

findings.title: Hardcoded Set for force sync slugs violates open-closed principle
findings.description: The service uses hardcoded Sets (forceParserSyncSlugs, forceDefaultParamsSyncSlugs) to track special-case slugs (lines 55-56). This requires code changes to add new special cases, violating the open-closed principle.
findings.snippet:
private readonly forceParserSyncSlugs = new Set<string>(["global_epu_index", "china_fx_gold_reserves", "macro_fx_sentiment"]);
private readonly forceDefaultParamsSyncSlugs = new Set<string>(["macro_fx_sentiment", "market_sentiment_usdx"]);
findings.suggested_issue: Move force sync configuration to the data definitions (akshare.definitions.ts) by adding optional flags like 'forceParserSync: true' to the definition interface.

findings.title: Chinese field names in data definitions reduce code portability
findings.description: The akshare.definitions.ts uses Chinese characters for field names (e.g., '开盘价', '最高价', '日期') which reduces code portability and may cause encoding issues in some environments.
findings.suggested_issue: This is acceptable as it matches the upstream AkShare API response field names. Consider adding English aliases in the label field for international display while keeping field names matching the API.

findings.title: NestJS module creates BullMQ instances directly instead of using @nestjs/bullmq
findings.description: The AkshareModule creates Queue and QueueEvents instances directly using useFactory (lines 31-50) instead of using the official @nestjs/bullmq module integration. This bypasses NestJS's built-in queue management and lifecycle hooks.
findings.suggested_issue: Consider migrating to @nestjs/bullmq module with BullModule.registerQueue() for better integration with NestJS lifecycle, health checks, and decorator-based job processing.

findings.title: Controller method lacks input validation for upgrade endpoint
findings.description: The AdminAkshareController.upgrade() method (lines 275-337) triggers a potentially destructive operation (gateway upgrade) without any confirmation mechanism or rate limiting. This could lead to accidental or malicious repeated upgrade attempts.
findings.suggested_issue: Add rate limiting (e.g., @Throttle decorator) and consider requiring a confirmation token or implementing a cooldown period between upgrade requests.

findings.title: Async void function for background task without error boundary
findings.description: The watchUpgradeCompletion() method is called with 'void' prefix (line 326) to run in background, but errors in this async function are only logged, not propagated. This could lead to silent failures in upgrade monitoring.
findings.suggested_issue: Consider using a dedicated background job queue (BullMQ) for upgrade monitoring instead of fire-and-forget async functions, ensuring proper error handling and retry logic.
